# S48 — The scope boundary is fragile prose, not a structured field

**Findings:** reproduced closing S47; a section edit silently dropped it · **Size: M** · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** additional marker configuration, prose append, or changes to the legacy markdown grammar.

## Why

The scope boundary — the `**Not in this slice:**` paragraph — is not a first-class part
of a slice. `promote` and `import` append the marker string to whatever section is *last*,
and `Slice.boundary()` finds it by scanning every section's prose for a paragraph that
starts with the marker. Three problems follow:

- **A section edit destroys it, silently.** Filing S47, `import` appended the boundary to
  its Git section; the next `slicer edit S47 --section Git` replaced that body and dropped
  the boundary, and `check` then warned that the scope was unbounded. Nothing re-adds it.
- Its position is arbitrary — "the last section", which differs slice to slice.
- `verify` detects it by scanning prose, so the check is only as reliable as the marker
  surviving in some body.

It should be set explicitly when a slice is created and stored as its own thing, so a
section edit cannot touch it — the boundary passed as an argument, not smuggled into prose.

## Failing tests

Boundary survives section replacement and append, reads old JSON without writing, persists on save, respects explicit clearing and custom/disabled markers, supports all edit sources and promotion overrides, remains visible/editable in the TUI, and preserves legacy byte-identity proof before canonical extraction.

## Implement

Store the full boundary paragraph in Slice.boundary, default empty, with backward-compatible loading at schema version 1. Extract the first configured-marker paragraph from old JSON only when the field is absent; read without writing and persist on the next save. Explicit fields, including empty, are authoritative. Share extraction with promotion, outline import and canonical migration conversion; keep legacy parsing and byte-identity proof unchanged. Seed promotion/import with cfg.boundary when absent. Migration preserves missing boundaries. Empty cfg.boundary disables extraction and warnings. Render after metadata before sections through the existing header. Verify the field. Add edit ID --boundary using existing sources/editor, mutually exclusive with --section; reject --append. Empty text clears. Add promote --boundary TEXT overriding source/default. All writes and logging go through ops.
